note: Literature establishes that DHX9 mutations cause neurodevelopmental disorders and CMT2 with seizures reported as a variable feature, making the quantitative frequency and comparison to other helicase encephalopathies highly plausible and test-worthy.

evidence.text: Calame et al. identified 20 individuals with de novo, ultra-rare heterozygous DHX9 variant alleles across a phenotypic spectrum ranging from neurodevelopmental disorders (mild to severe) to axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, noting seizures among the clinical findings.

source.title: Monoallelic variation in DHX9, the gene encoding the DExH-box helicase DHX9, underlies neurodevelopment disorders and Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease
source.quote: Using exome sequencing and family-based rare-variant analyses, we identified 20 individuals with de novo, ultra-rare, heterozygous missense or loss-of-function (LoF) DHX9 variant alleles. Phenotypes ranged from NDDs to the distal symmetric polyneuropathy axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT2).

evidence.text: Review of DEAD- and DExH-box RNA helicases notes clinical heterogeneity including ADHD, seizures, abnormal muscle tone, and motor disabilities across helicase-related neurodevelopmental disorders, specifically referencing DHX9.

source.title: The role of DEAD-and DExH-box RNA helicases in neurodevelopmental disorders
